claude.performance_metric: continued store contraction under private ownership: 46 Sears + 29 Kmart closures announced in 2021 (Coresight); no public audited outcome record
claude.rationale: The slice documents only that the acquired going concern passed to a private buyer (Transformco) and that Sears Holdings ceased periodic reporting (last 10-K FY2017; Form 15 filed April 2019), so there is no audited outcome record for the 2022-2024 window. The single traceable realized signal — 46 announced Sears and 29 Kmart closures in 2021 — reflects continued footprint contraction but does not specify disruption at the product/process interface (p4) or a process/organization fracture (p5). With no evidence isolating either interface, both are coded uncertain rather than 0, consistent with the slice's own UNCERTAIN outcome coding.

gemini.performance_metric: continued contraction of the acquired store base
gemini.rationale: The slice explicitly states that because the going-concern business passed to a private affiliate and ceased public reporting, there is no public audited outcome record for the ~2022-2024 window, making the outcome uncertain. There is no documented evidence of product/process or process/organization fracture, only press reports of continued store closures.

grok.performance_metric: continued store-base contraction (46 Sears + 29 Kmart closures in 2021); no audited public outcome
grok.rationale: The slice documents only continued retail-footprint contraction under private ownership (Coresight tallies of 46 Sears and 29 Kmart closures in 2021) and the absence of any public audited financials after the Form 15. No realized-outcome evidence is given of product/process interface misalignment (p4) or of operations fracturing against organization/culture (p5); absence of such documentation is therefore coded 0 for both pathways.
